paper_id: Mitigating Redundant Data Transfers for Mobile Web Applications via App-Specific Cache Space
title: Mitigating Redundant Data Transfers for Mobile Web Applications via App-Specific Cache Space
motivation: Mobile Web apps suffer from redundant transfers causing traffic waste, slow load, energy drain; current cache mechanisms are far from satisfactory
problem_framing: How to accurately identify stable resources that can be packaged and loaded locally for long periods to reduce redundant transfers
key_insight: Native apps control resources explicitly via packages; Web apps should adopt similar app-specific resource management instead of relying on shared browser cache
method_signature: ReWAP packages stable resources with engine-generated manifest, uses HTML5 AppCache wrapper for app-specific local storage
evaluation_criteria: Traffic savings vs original cache-enabled apps, runtime overhead, page load time for cold/warm starts
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Page load time does not always improve due to checking update with server-side components; energy drain not addressed
evidence_for_taste: cache policies is not a desirable mechanism
app-specific logics to control the resources
the variance of saved data traffic is significantly large
using cache policies is not a desirable mechanism
thinking_moves: Borrow mechanism design from native apps to solve Web cache failures
Frame the problem as app-specific resource management rather than browser-level cache tuning
Measure actual cache hit gaps before proposing solution
Normalize resources with same content but different URLs into single entity
Predict update time using gradient descent on evolution history
Leverage existing HTML5 standards (AppCache) for easy deployment
cites_own_work: Measurement and analysis of mobile web cache performance (WWW 2016)
Demystifying the imperfect client-side cache performance of mobile web browsing
